transformations: Twitter: `id` stored as float in source -> precision lost (35453 unique of 56571). Never used as a key; a new row key `pid` is assigned.
Twitter: `date` parsed as m/d/Y H:M and treated as UTC (archive convention; minute precision only).

Twitter: 9877 rows flagged isRetweet plus 127 unflagged rows starting 'RT @' treated as retweets. Their like counts belong to the original author, so they are excluded from authorship and engagement analysis (kept in counts).
Twitter: 20 device strings mapped to Android / iPhone / Web / Staff tools (TweetDeck, Media Studio, Ads) / Other.
Twitter: 761 own posts have 0 likes, concentrated in 2012-13 @-replies (94% replies) -> treated as a collection artefact and excluded from engagement metrics; a sensitivity run keeps them.
Truth Social: `is_retruth` is False for all 32754 rows although 5933 posts begin 'RT @'/'RT:' -> field judged broken and ignored; reposts re-derived from text.
Truth Social: 1020 'RT: <link>' posts carry his own added comment (quote posts) and real likes; kept as a separate post type in his own words.
Truth Social: `emotion` = 'unknown' for every row -> dropped. Emotion re-scored with the NRC lexicon.
Truth Social: 892 posts had double-encoded characters (e.g. 'â€™'); repaired with ftfy.
Truth Social: textless posts (media/video) kept for frequency and engagement, excluded from text NLP.
Truth Social: multi-label fields joined by '|' (topic, rhetorical_device, sentiment_toward_target) split; first label kept as primary for comparison.
Truth Social: 89% of re-posts show 0 likes (the platform credits engagement to the original post), so re-posts are excluded from engagement analysis, as on Twitter.
Truth Social: 10 own posts with 0 likes excluded from engagement metrics as likely collection artefacts.
Truth Social: 73 posts in the final 3 days before collection excluded from engagement metrics (counts still accruing).
All timestamps converted to US Eastern for time-of-day analysis.

Relative Performance (RP) = likes / median likes of the same platform's eligible posts in the previous 30 days (min 20 posts); a time window is robust to posting bursts. When he posted fewer than 20 times in 30 days (2009-11), the median of his previous 50 posts is used instead. Secondary: RP_period = likes / platform-period median. Likes are a count, not a rate: there is no impressions denominator.
